title: AI reviewers favored confident wording in matched research papers
summary: In a 504-paper experiment, all six model reviewers more often gave higher scores to rewrites with confident wording. Claude Sonnet 4.6 favored the confident version in 40% of pairs and the less confident version in 6%, with 54% tied. Researchers checked text similarity and wording shifts before comparing evaluations.
ai_technology: Claude Sonnet 4.6; GPT-5.5; Gemini; Gemma; Qwen; GLM
organization: CISPA Helmholtz Center for Information Security; German Research Center for Artificial Intelligence; University of Technology Nuremberg; Inria

source_review.scope: v1 paired rewrite checks and 504-paper comparative review experiment, Table 4

evidence.tested: Each model independently evaluated one rewrite at a time for each pair under standardized review instructions. The study checked style manipulation and content similarity on the rewritten manuscripts.
evidence.unknown: Rewriting can introduce small uncontrolled meaning changes. The experiment concerns model scores and does not measure actual conference decisions.
evidence.ai_role: Language models generated matched high- and low-confidence prose variants and six model reviewers independently scored the rewritten versions.
